text: dsh-openrouter-guardrails 是一个适用于 DSH Web、桌面和 CLI 配置的模型路由插件。它读取 OpenRouter 路由的凭据，定期查询该密钥可使用的模型，并通过 DSH settings 更新模型列表；已在本地模型目录中的模型保留目录信息，目录尚未收录的模型会放入单独路由。同步会在启动、凭据变更和定时间隔触发，也会记录同步状态。适合需要让模型选择器反映 OpenRouter 密钥权限的用户。使用前需配置 OpenRouter 账户、路由和凭据。

dsh-openrouter-guardrails filters DSH OpenRouter model lists to models allowed by the configured key. It syncs at startup, after credential changes, and periodically. Catalogued models stay on the original route; others use a separate route. Requires an OpenRouter account and credential.
让 DSH 的 OpenRouter 模型列表只显示我的密钥能用的模型。
OpenRouter 账户权限变了，怎么自动刷新 DSH 的模型选项？
Keep my DSH OpenRouter model picker in sync with the models available to my key.
dsh-openrouter-guardrails 的功能「按密钥同步模型」：启动时、OpenRouter 路由凭据更新后及定时触发同步；查询该凭据可用模型，并将已收录模型写入原路由的模型列表。
dsh-openrouter-guardrails 的功能「补充目录外模型」：同步时把本地目录未描述但可服务的模型转换为模型条目，放入单独的 OpenRouter 兼容路由；不再需要时移除该路由。
dsh-openrouter-guardrails 使用前须知：插件会把配置路由的 API 凭据作为 Bearer 凭据发送到该路由的 baseURL，查询 /models/user；默认服务为 openrouter.ai。
dsh-openrouter-guardrails 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 6 天；提交数 1；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · dsh-openrouter-guardrails：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that makes the OpenRouter model picker show **only the models your API key may use**, the way Claude Code and pi do.

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · dsh-openrouter-guardrails：If an OpenRouter [guardrail](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/guardrails.md) limits your key to 10 models, DSH still lists the ~400 models of its bundled catalog, and anything outside the allowlist fails with a 403. This plugin asks OpenRouter which models the key may use, [`GET /api/v1/models/user`](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/models/list-models-filtered-by-user-provider-preferences-privacy-settings-and-guardrails.md) (filtered by guardrails, privacy settings, and provider preferences), and writes exactly that list into your profile.
dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · dsh-openrouter-guardrails：Background: [deepseek-harness#12355](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/12355).

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · What it changes：| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `openrouter` lists the whole bundled catalog (396 chat models in 0.2.2-rc.1) | `openrouter` lists the allowed models the bundled catalog describes |
| Allowed models newer than the bundled catalog are missing | They appear under a second group, **OpenRouter (new models)** |

The plugin writes two things through DSH's settings service, and nothing else:

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · What it changes：- `providers.openrouter.models`: the allowed models the bundled catalog already describes, as bare `{ id }` entries. They inherit every catalog fact, **including their own wire protocol**, so OpenRouter's Claude models keep `anthropic-messages`.
- `providers.openrouter-guardrails`: a declared `openai-completions` route, with the same key and base URL, for allowed models the bundled catalog does not describe yet. `llm-pi-ai` lets only a route, not a model, name a protocol, and the OpenRouter catalog mixes two, so these models cannot share the first route without changing the protocol of every model on it. Their context window, output cap, input modalities, reasoning levels, and compatibility switches come from the `/models/user` response. The route is removed when no such model is left.

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · What it changes：Your route settings (`apiKeyEnv`, `baseURL`, `api`, headers, …) are never touched. If the route sets its own `api`, every model already uses it, so all allowed models go on that one route and no second route is created.

Every write is validated by `llm-pi-ai` before it is saved; a write it cannot serve is refused as a whole and the profile stays as it was.

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · Install：Requirements: DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`, and an OpenRouter route configured with an API key (Settings → Models → OpenRouter), which gives a profile entry like:

```yaml
- id: llm-pi-ai
  name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai"
  config:
    providers:

Then install the plugin from GitHub:

- **Desktop app**: Plugins page → install from `github:EamonnLiu/dsh-openrouter-guardrails`.
- **CLI / web profiles**: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:EamonnLiu/dsh-openrouter-guardrails`
dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · Install：The first pass runs a few seconds after the plugin loads; the picker updates live.
dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · Configuration：All optional, set on the plugin's entry (`id: openrouter-guardrails`) in `cordis.patch.yml`:

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | `openrouter` | The `llm-pi-ai` route to narrow |
| `extraProvider` | `openrouter-guardrails` | Route id this plugin owns for models newer than the catalog |
| `extraDisplayName` | `OpenRouter (new models)` | Picker label of that route |
| `intervalHours` | `6` | Refresh interval |
| `timeoutMs` | `30000` | `/models/user` request timeout |
| `startupGraceMs` | `30000` | How long startup waits for `llm-pi-ai` |

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · Status and troubleshooting：Each pass writes `~/.dsh/cache/openrouter-guardrails.json` (or `$DSH_HOME/cache/…`) with the outcome and the ids it wrote; it never contains the key.

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · Status and troubleshooting：| `reason` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `route-missing` | No `providers.openrouter` route is configured |
| `no-key` | The route names no `apiKeyEnv`, or the credential is not set |
| `unauthorized` | OpenRouter refused the key (401/403); nothing was changed |
| `fetch-failed` | Network error or non-2xx response; nothing was changed |
| `empty-result` | The key may use no servable model; nothing was changed |
| `model-overrides-present` | The route uses `modelOverrides`, which `llm-pi-ai` refuses beside a `models` list |
| `extra-route-conflict` | `extraProvider` names a provider the bundled catalog ships |
| `settings-write-failed` | `llm-pi-ai` refused the write; `detail` says why |

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · Status and troubleshooting：Known limitation: if none of the allowed models is in the bundled catalog, the `openrouter` route cannot be narrowed to zero models (an empty `models` list means "the whole catalog" to `llm-pi-ai`); the allowed models still appear under the second route.

Do not run this beside [`dsh-openrouter-sync-models`](https://github.com/m1khal3v/dsh-openrouter-sync-models); both write the same `models` list.

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · Uninstall：Remove the plugin, then delete `models` under `providers.openrouter` and the `providers.openrouter-guardrails` route (Settings → Models, or `cordis.patch.yml`). The plugin cannot do this itself, because it cannot tell an uninstall from a reload.

dsh-openrouter-guardrails README · Development：Plain ESM JavaScript with no dependencies and no build step.

```sh
npm test   # node --test; add --test-isolation=none where child processes are restricted
```

The HMR-context escape in `lib/hmr.js` follows [`dsh-openrouter-sync-models`](https://github.com/m1khal3v/dsh-openrouter-sync-models) (MIT).
